title: Descent of an invariant tensor comparison and finite local freeness
statement:
Let $C\subset A$ be an inclusion of commutative rings, let $B$ be a commutative ring, and let $\sigma,\tau:A\to B$ agree on $C$. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is surjective [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $\phi:A\otimes_C A\to B$, $a\otimes a'\mapsto\sigma(a)\tau(a')$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Suppose there are finitely many $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that $B_{\sigma(f_i)}$ is finite free over $A_{f_i}$ via $\sigma$; localizations are taken by powers of the indicated element. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$, suppose there is a faithfully flat map $C_{\mathfrak p}\to D_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] such that $A\otimes_C D_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finite free $D_{\mathfrak p}$-module and
$$\phi_{D_{\mathfrak p}}:(A\otimes_C D_{\mathfrak p})\otimes_{D_{\mathfrak p}}(A\otimes_C D_{\mathfrak p})\longrightarrow B\otimes_C D_{\mathfrak p}$$
is an isomorphism. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism, and $C\to A$ is flat and faithfully flat. The $C$-module $A$ is finitely presented, meaning there is an exact sequence $C^m\to C^n\to A\to0$ for finite $m,n$, and is finite projective, meaning a direct summand of a finite free $C$-module. There are finitely many $g_1,\ldots,g_l\in C$ generating the unit ideal with $A_{g_i}$ finite free over $C_{g_i}$. The structural map $q:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and surjective. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}T$ in $\operatorname{Spec}C$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_C T)$, whose coordinate ring is finite as a $T$-module. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism with its two projections equal to $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: For every C-module M and prime p, realize its localization as C_p ⊗_C M, using the canonical map m ↦ 1 ⊗ m. Scalar cancellation identifies D_p ⊗_{C_p} (C_p ⊗_C M) with D_p ⊗_C M, naturally in M. Tensor symmetry conjugates the stated map φ ⊗ id_{D_p} to id_{D_p} ⊗ φ. These are the maps and identifications used below; the tensor-square reidentification is already incorporated in the hypothesis as stated in Lean.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property; Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module), fraction construction; scalar identifications used in Tag 03BM.

proof.text: Apply faithful-flat reflection of bijectivity to the C_p-linear base change of φ. The further D_p-base change is conjugate to id_{D_p} ⊗ φ by scalar cancellation and is bijective by the hypothesis and tensor symmetry. Thus every maximal localization is bijective. The local bijectivity criterion, with C_p ⊗_C (A ⊗_C A) and C_p ⊗_C B as localization models, proves that φ is bijective. AlgEquiv.ofBijective gives its algebra inverse.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), second proof paragraph, descent of the comparison; algebra.tex Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local).

proof.text: The free D_p-module D_p ⊗_C A is flat. Scalar cancellation identifies this with D_p ⊗_{C_p} (C_p ⊗_C A), so faithful-flat descent makes C_p ⊗_C A flat over C_p. Localization of scalars makes it flat over C. Apply the local flatness criterion to the canonical maps A → C_p ⊗_C A to get flatness over C. Surjectivity of Spec A → Spec C then gives faithful flatness.

source.place: Tag 03BM, second proof paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 03C4 (lemma-descend-properties-modules), (3), 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), (6), and 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: Regard $B$ as an $A$-module through $\sigma$. Its localization at $f_i\in A$ is $B_{\sigma(f_i)}$: the fraction $b/f_i^r$ corresponds to $b/\sigma(f_i)^r$. The given $f_i$ generate the unit ideal of $A$, and these localized modules are finite free by hypothesis. The standard-cover lemma [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-presentation-flat] therefore makes $B$ a finitely presented $A$-module. Step 2 identifies it with $A\otimes_C A$ as an $A$-module through the FIRST factor, since $\phi((ra)\otimes a')=\sigma(r)\phi(a\otimes a')$. Apply MODULE finite-presentation descent [lem-trf-finite-presentation-module-descent-flat-local] with $R=C$, $T=A$, $M=A$. Its faithful-flatness hypothesis is step 3, and its scalar extension $T\otimes_R M$ is this first-factor module. Thus $A$ is finitely presented as a $C$-module, giving the asserted finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00EO (lemma-cover), finite presentation; Tag 03C4 (lemma-descend-properties-modules), (2); used exactly this way in groupoids.tex Tag 03BM.

proof.text: Finitely presented flat modules are projective. Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective chooses a surjection C^r → A and a section A → C^r by the projective lifting property, giving the required explicit retract. The finite-projective standard-free-cover theorem then gives finitely many g_i spanning the unit ideal with finite free localized modules.

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), (1) implies (2), (3), (7); explicit splitting uses Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective).

proof.text: The global finite presentation of A as a C-module implies finiteness as a module and finite presentation as an algebra (Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.ModuleFinitePresentation). The affine Spec criteria for finite morphisms, flat morphisms and locally finitely presented morphisms therefore apply directly to q. Together these give the asserted IsFiniteLocallyFree structure. Surjectivity is exactly the assumed surjectivity of the map on prime spectra. This uses no restriction to the standard free cover.

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), affine finite-free implication; Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local); Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: For any C-algebra T, pullback symmetry followed by pullbackSpecIso C T A gives the required isomorphism to Spec (T ⊗_C A). The two pullbackSpecIso projection identities give exactly includeRight and algebraMap T. Finiteness of T ⊗_C A over T is the base-change instance for finite modules. The argument works for every C-algebra T, so in particular for every affine open in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), affine base change; algebra.tex Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), bilinearity and pure-tensor generation.

proof.text: Apply the affine fibre-product formula once more with both algebras equal to $A$. Step 2 and contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ give an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}A$. The two projections are induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Composing these ring maps with $\phi$ gives $a\mapsto\sigma(a)\tau(1)=\sigma(a)$ and $a\mapsto\sigma(1)\tau(a)=\tau(a)$, respectively, so their scheme morphisms are exactly $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\tau$.
